D018-D020_h001.question: It’s been a rough few weeks since the incident at school, doctor. I keep having these awful dreams, always variations of that day, waking up in a cold sweat. Honestly, it’s hard to even get out of bed some mornings, let alone lead a high school. The drive to tackle my usual work has just… vanished. And the smallest decisions, what to wear, what to have for dinner, feel monumental. My husband gets frustrated, but I just freeze. I find myself replaying everything, focusing on how certain parents or even some of my staff reacted, feeling like if they’d just done things differently, maybe none of this would have happened. And the shame, it’s just relentless. Every time I think about it, my heart pounds, and it takes forever to calm down. I just feel… stuck.

    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D020_h002.question: I'm here because things just feel... off, you know? It's been about three weeks now, maybe a month. It's like I can’t stop thinking, "If only I'd checked that machine one more time" – like it was somehow my fault. I’m constantly on edge, like something terrible is about to happen, especially with the noises at work. Every time there’s a sudden clatter or bang on the line, I jump out of my skin. D018-D020_h003.question:
"Honestly, Doc, I've just been… off. It's been a few weeks, maybe a month since that call. When I even think about it, my heart starts pounding and I get this sickening knot in my stomach, just like I’m right back there. Nothing really feels good anymore. Things I used to enjoy, like playing ball or even just grabbing a beer with the guys, it all just feels flat. I can't even crack a smile most days.

And I find myself snapping at everyone, especially after that night. I know it’s not right, but I keep replaying it and thinking, if only *they* had done things differently, maybe it wouldn't have gone down that way. I just can't shake this feeling of responsibility, like it was all my fault, even though I know I followed procedure.

It’s even the little things. Deciding what to eat for lunch can feel like a monumental task, and I just freeze. And on patrol, any sudden movement on the street, even a car door slamming, makes me jump out of my skin. I'm constantly on edge, always expecting something to happen."

    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D020_h006.question:
It’s been… a few weeks now, maybe a month since the salon fire. I keep seeing flashes of it, you know? Not like real, full-blown movies, but snippets – the smoke, the heat. And honestly, it's exhausting trying not to think about it. If I let my mind wander, it just goes back there.

The worst part is, I can't even remember clear chunks of it. Like, I recall getting everyone out, but bits and pieces are just… gone. It’s like a puzzle with missing pieces. And everything just feels flat. I try to feel happy, or even sad, and there’s just… nothing. Like my feelings are all blocked up. The weirdest things get to me now too. Just the other day, one of my stylists tapped my shoulder to ask a question and I nearly jumped out of my skin, screaming. And then there’s the anger. It just bubbles up out of nowhere, over the tiniest things that never used to bother me. I really need to get back to work, but I just… can't. Not feeling like this.

A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D020_h006.answer: A & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D018-D020_h007.question:
Honestly, I’m just not myself. It’s been… well, a few weeks now, maybe a month since what happened at the office. Things just keep playing over in my head, snippets of it, especially that moment with the files. I try so hard not to think about it, to avoid talking about work when I get home, or even looking at the news, but it’s always there.

My husband tries to be understanding. He’ll put his arm around me, and I just… jump. It’s not him, truly, but any sudden touch just makes me flinch. And I’ve been so snappy. The other day, my daughter asked a simple question about dinner, and I just bit her head off, shouting about how I’m not a short-order cook. I feel terrible about it later, but in the moment, it's just raw anger.

The toughest part, I think, is I feel so distant from everyone. My husband will say, "I love you," and I hear the words, but it’s like I can’t feel it back. It’s just… empty. And what happened itself, it’s not a complete picture in my mind. There are gaps, bits I just can’t recall, even though other parts are crystal clear, almost too clear. I know it’s affecting my work, and frankly, my whole life.
D018-D020_h007.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D020_h007.answer: A & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder
